title: SAFe explained: from teams to enterprise

slides.title: Why SAFe exists
slides.narration: Agile works for one team. The hard problem is coordination: many teams, shared dependencies, one business outcome. The Scaled Agile Framework, or SAFe, is one answer. This is a plain-language tour for technical newcomers. No certification pitch, no endorsement. Claims are attributed to Scaled Agile's published pages, accessed November 10, 2026.

slides.title: SAFe today: Core and AI-Native
bullets: Homepage distinguishes Core SAFe and AI-Native SAFe
slides.narration: The framework evolves. As of November 2026, the Scaled Agile homepage distinguishes Core SAFe, their long-standing operating model for scaling Lean and Agile, from AI-Native SAFe, released in 2026. The SAFe 6.0 configurations page points readers toward the latest version. So what follows is SAFe 6.0 context, not a claim about what is newest. Always check the official site and access dates.

slides.title: The ART and the Planning Interval
bullets: Agile Release Train: long-lived team of teams
PI Planning aligns teams; value flows on demand
slides.narration: The heart of SAFe is the Agile Release Train, or ART: a long-lived team of Agile teams aligned to a value stream. Work is organized in a Planning Interval, or PI, a timebox of eight to twelve weeks. Distinguish two things: synchronized PI planning, where teams align on objectives for the interval; and releasing value, which is not tied to that cadence. Solutions release continuously or on demand, whenever ready.

slides.title: Four configurations (SAFe 6.0 context)
bullets: Large Solution: big systems, no portfolio layer
Portfolio / Full: strategy and funding at scale
slides.narration: SAFe 6.0, released March 2023, defined four configurations. Essential SAFe is the foundation: ARTs, roles, events, artifacts. Large Solution coordinates very large solutions beyond one ART, without a portfolio layer. Portfolio SAFe adds strategy, funding, and lean portfolio management. Full SAFe combines all layers for the largest enterprises. This is 6.0 context, not an assertion that 6.0 is current.

slides.title: What the evidence does (and doesn't) say
bullets: Adoption surveys exist but vary in method
Vendor research is directional, not independent
slides.narration: What does the evidence show? Scaled Agile publishes adoption research, and the State of Agile report series discusses SAFe usage, but the instruments, denominators, and years differ, and figures are easy to misquote. I will not put a percentage on screen without the original and its denominator. Vendor research reports adopter benefits; treat it as directional. The defensible claim is narrow: SAFe is widely adopted and structured, and outcomes depend on how it is applied.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Start with Essential; add layers on need
slides.narration: Key takeaways. Start with Essential SAFe and the ART; add large-solution or portfolio layers only when you have the problem they solve. Plan together in the Planning Interval; release value continuously or on demand. Treat the framework as a starting hypothesis, not a guarantee. Measure outcomes, not ceremony compliance. This video is educational, not certification, training, or endorsement by Scaled Agile. For detail, use the official framework site, linked with access dates in the sources.
